nodes.label: Stack choice: Python3 + PyGObject/GTK3
nodes.rationale: GTK3 Python bindings already ship on Ubuntu desktop, so this adds zero new system packages vs Electron/Qt which would need a new runtime (ponytail rung 4/5).

nodes.label: apt-mark showmanual over full dpkg list
nodes.rationale: dpkg-query -l lists 1000+ dependency packages; apt-mark showmanual is apt's own definition of user-chosen software and also surfaces dpkg -i .deb installs.

nodes.label: Risk heuristic, not a dependency graph
nodes.rationale: Full apt-cache rdepends per package would make the scan slow; risk is instead read off fields the single dpkg-query call already returns (Essential/Priority).

nodes.label: Privilege escalation: pkexec, not sudo
nodes.rationale: pkexec is the standard PolicyKit GUI prompt already on every Ubuntu desktop (same one GNOME Software uses) so no new dependency and no password touches the app process.

nodes.label: Wine detection: parse prefix registry files directly
nodes.rationale: Wine has no central app database; parsing system.reg/user.reg text directly with a regex is faster and avoids spinning up a Wine process just to list apps.

nodes.label: Leftover scan is name-matching, not a package-manager feature
nodes.rationale: There is no manifest for runtime-created config/cache dirs, so leftovers are found by case-insensitive name-matching and always shown before deletion (FR5).

nodes.label: Pure logic vs. subprocess boundary
nodes.rationale: Each backend splits scan()/uninstall() (shells out) from pure parse_*/classify_* functions, so tests can cover parsing/risk logic without a live system.

nodes.label: Installer: copy + launcher script, not pip/venv
nodes.rationale: A venv needs --system-site-packages for GTK3 bindings and buys nothing since there are zero pip dependencies; install.sh needs no root and is what a contributor runs.

nodes.label: GUI fix: blank-window bug (show_all())
nodes.rationale: self.add(self._build_ui()) was never followed by self.show_all(); in GTK3 present() only maps the toplevel, not its children.

nodes.label: GUI progress feedback: spinner + progress bar
nodes.rationale: A Gtk.Spinner covers scanning and one Gtk.ProgressBar updated via GLib.idle_add covers uninstalling, since GTK widgets can't be touched off the main thread.

nodes.label: App icon: hand-written SVG hourglass 'A'
nodes.rationale: Plain XML hand-drawn icon avoids an icon-editor or Pillow dependency (ponytail rung 3: stdlib/text suffices).

nodes.label: Light/dark toggle via gtk-application-prefer-dark-theme
nodes.rationale: Flips the same switch GNOME's own dark-mode setting flips so every widget reacts correctly with zero theme-specific styling.

nodes.label: Fix: theme toggle no-op on split light/dark theme names
nodes.rationale: Themes like Zorin ship light/dark as two unrelated names the boolean property doesn't touch; fixed by scanning theme dirs and setting gtk-theme-name directly.

nodes.label: Fix: app icon missing from dock/taskbar
nodes.rationale: Wayland tags windows by the GTK application-id, not process name; the .desktop file must be named after that same id or it falls back to a generic icon.

nodes.label: Icon redesign: bezier strokes instead of text glyphs
nodes.rationale: Typed <text> glyphs render however the target's font stack resolves; replaced with hand-authored cubic-bezier strokes for a guaranteed, font-independent silhouette.

nodes.label: Fix: progress bar had no visible motion
nodes.rationale: fraction was only set at start/end of each item's slot; fixed with a GLib.timeout_add crawl toward 92% then a snap to the boundary on completion.

nodes.label: Displayed app name shortened to 'The Uninstaller'
nodes.rationale: Window title, GLib.set_application_name and the .desktop Name= are the three places the UI-facing name shows; project/repo name was left unchanged.

nodes.label: Leftover cleanup shows bytes freed
nodes.rationale: Size must be measured with path_size() before rmtree/unlink runs since a deleted tree reports 0 bytes afterward; format_size centralized in models.py.

nodes.label: Fix: apt nonzero exit doesn't mean files remain
nodes.rationale: A broken postrm script can make apt-get purge report failure forever even though dpkg already removed the files; AptBackend now falls back to dpkg's status field.

nodes.label: Freed-space total includes the app itself, not just leftovers
nodes.rationale: When an app leaves zero leftovers the earlier freed-space message never fired; fixed by summing app.size_bytes over every successfully-uninstalled app.

nodes.label: SRS is Markdown, not a binary PDF, in version control
nodes.rationale: A PDF can't be diffed or reviewed in a PR; SRS.md is the source of truth, exported to PDF on demand via pandoc rather than adding a PDF-generation dependency.

nodes.label: Release artifact is a git archive tarball
nodes.rationale: Pure Python with no compile step, so git archive from the signed-off tag honours .gitignore automatically and needs no packaging toolchain on the release machine.

nodes.label: License: MIT
nodes.rationale: Chosen over GPL-3.0 for a small utility meant to be copied/forked/packaged by distro maintainers without friction; no competitive moat to defend.

nodes.label: Packaging: staged tree and dpkg-deb
nodes.rationale: dpkg-deb --build with no debhelper/dh_make/debian-rules apparatus, since this is one arch-independent Python package with four install locations.

nodes.label: Stitches (Linux 0.2)
The rename: The Uninstaller -> SoftHUB -> Stitches
nodes.rationale: src/uninstaller -> src/stitches, app id io.github.stitches; a rename unpins GNOME taskbar favorites keyed by .desktop filename, so install.sh rewrites that list.

nodes.label: Window: sidebar + stack, one module per page
nodes.rationale: Gtk.StackSidebar can't carry an icon and count badge per row, so a custom Gtk.ListBox row is used; each tool became its own module under pages/.

nodes.label: The line loader
nodes.rationale: A Gtk.ProgressBar restyled to a 3px glowing line, since apt/snap/fwupd/e4defrag report no readable progress; reuses the 0.1 crawl-to-92%-then-snap approach.

nodes.label: shell.py: C locale, nothing on stdin
nodes.rationale: apt/flatpak/snap translate the exact strings parsers match under a non-English locale, so shell.output() forces LC_ALL=C and empty stdin to avoid tools hanging.

nodes.label: Updates (APT, Snap, Flatpak, GitHub AppImages)
nodes.rationale: Four sources checked in parallel via ThreadPoolExecutor; APT/Snap batch per password prompt, AppImages compared by size via the .upd_info ELF section.

nodes.label: Cleanup (APT cache, Snap revisions, caches, Trash, etc.)
nodes.rationale: Unused Flatpak runtimes are listed by asking flatpak itself rather than reimplementing its dependency knowledge; nothing pre-selected, confirmation always required.

nodes.label: Drivers (ubuntu-drivers, fwupd/LVFS, linux-firmware)
nodes.rationale: Linux drivers mostly update with the kernel; the page lists the three separate update sources rather than pretending to a Windows-style driver catalogue.

nodes.label: Defrag (ext4/btrfs/XFS online defragmenters)
nodes.rationale: Every drive is listed with a reason when it won't be touched (SSD, unmounted, unsupported fs); no Analyze step because e4defrag -c needs root to report anything.

nodes.label: Second round: Home, numbers with a verdict
nodes.rationale: Every reading carries Good/Warning/Critical and every BIOS setting a plain sentence; facts come from files any user can read, so sysinfo.describe_firmware is pure and testable.

nodes.label: UDisks2 through busctl --json, not Gio
nodes.rationale: Fetched via busctl rather than gi.repository.Gio so vitals.py/diagnose.py import nothing from GObject and their tests run on CI without PyGObject.

nodes.label: Diagnose: Windows tools, mapped to Linux equivalents
nodes.rationale: Every check reads without a password (dpkg --verify, apt-get check with Debug::NoLocking=1); Diagnose waits for an explicit Scan instead of auto-scanning.

nodes.label: Drivers: a 'What it is' purpose column
nodes.rationale: Rows like 'KEK CA' explain nothing on their own, so each fwupd/linux-firmware/kernel row got a plain-language purpose mapped by plugin.

nodes.label: Stitches lists itself via local_backend.py
nodes.rationale: A per-user install.sh install lives under ~/.local, invisible to any package manager, so a fifth backend recognises this app's own install layout under current and past names.

nodes.label: Themes: Light, Dark, AMOLED, Glass
nodes.rationale: Light/Dark follow the system theme; AMOLED/Glass are extra CSS a priority above base CSS; Glass is translucency (RGBA visual), not blur, since GTK3 can't blur behind a window.

nodes.label: Update all (removed in the fifth round)
nodes.rationale: Two buttons that both updated everything read as a choice that isn't one; the select-all circle already does the same in two clicks.

nodes.label: Self-update from GitHub releases
nodes.rationale: selfupdate.py checks api.github.com releases/latest at startup; install method is decided from the running copy's own path (.deb vs install.sh vs git checkout).

nodes.label: Releasing is pushing a tag
nodes.rationale: linux-build.yml builds the .deb and tarball on a v* tag; each job tries gh release create first so the first to finish wins instead of clobbering SHA256SUMS.

nodes.label: Real screenshots without the screenshot portal
nodes.rationale: GNOME's screenshot APIs refuse a non-interactive caller; Gtk.Widget.draw() onto a cairo surface renders the real running window from inside the process, Wayland included.

nodes.label: Third round: dock instead of sidebar
nodes.rationale: A Gtk.RadioButton group with draw_indicator=False renders as plain buttons with :checked on the open tool, so exactly one stays lit with no selection code.

nodes.label: The sewn logo (catch-stitch dashed strokes)
nodes.rationale: stroke-dasharray on the A-over-V curves plus a dashed border reads as thread between needle holes; straight-line and over/under-gap variants were tried and dropped.

nodes.label: Compact Home: three columns on one screen
nodes.rationale: Everything fits the default 1180x760 window without scrolling; a compact CSS class sets smaller labels on Home only, other pages keep their size.

nodes.label: Fourth round fix: icon not showing (icon-cache mtime)
nodes.rationale: GTK/Shell only rescans an icon theme when the theme's top folder mtime changes, not a scalable/apps subfolder; install.sh now touches the top folder.

nodes.label: Fourth round fix: dashes not reading as stitches
nodes.rationale: Round caps as wide as the gaps closed every gap at dock size; fixed with square caps, a 9-on/6-off pattern sized so a stitch lands on both tips and the apex.

nodes.label: Dock groups and mixed window/dock themes
nodes.rationale: The window and dock each pick one of four themes independently; _apply_theme writes both settings before moving any radio to avoid a callback loop.

nodes.label: Home: cards sized to content, not stretched
nodes.rationale: A GTK3 container fixes its size-request mode on first measurement; empty grids before readings arrive settled on the wrong mode, fixed with a 'Reading...' placeholder from the start.

nodes.label: Diagnose shows its output as it happens (Terminal panel)
nodes.rationale: shell.output()/run() take on_line callbacks streaming each line via GLib.idle_add, so every command and its result is visible live, not just a final verdict.

nodes.label: One select-all circle, nothing ticked at first
nodes.rationale: The ticks' column header holds a tri-state checkbox (ticked/dash/empty) instead of separate select all/none/safe buttons; meaning of 'all' is per-page (filtered rows, non-critical only).

nodes.label: Cleanup says what it touches
nodes.rationale: A card/line states only rebuildable or re-downloadable things are removed; each location's reason column was reworded to say whether personal data is involved.

nodes.label: Drivers: a Released column and a source icon
nodes.rationale: Release date is read per-source (changelog for APT/kernel, LVFS Created for fwupd, DMI bios_date fallback); the source moved into a clickable icon column.

nodes.label: Defrag: tiles grouped by OS
nodes.rationale: Partitions are grouped Linux/Windows/macOS/Boot/Other via the GPT PARTTYPENAME lsblk reports, each a Gtk.FlowBox tile with drive icon, name, device and status.

nodes.label: Update notice: 4 seconds, line running down
nodes.rationale: _TOAST_SECONDS cut from 10 to 4; ActionBar.countdown() shrinks the bar's line timed against GLib.get_monotonic_time() so it doesn't drift.

nodes.label: Fifth round: the dock logo is the Home button
nodes.rationale: HomePage has no separate icon; _dock_button gives the icon-less page the logo at the same size as every other dock icon.

nodes.label: Fifth round: own icons with theme stand-ins
nodes.rationale: No standard icon name exists for 'uninstall an app', so custom symbolic SVGs were drawn and appended as a search path after the icon theme, serving as stand-ins where a theme lacks an icon.

nodes.label: Fifth round: Home as groups, not cards
nodes.rationale: Cards removed in favour of a small accent icon and title over each grid; spacing between groups replaces borders as the visual separator.

nodes.label: Fifth round: Cleanup as one table with a filter
nodes.rationale: The explanation card and Risk column are gone; the risk tag moved to the end of the reason text, and a location filter (Safe/Caution/No password) was added like Updates.

nodes.label: Fifth round: Drivers drops the update log, no Update all
nodes.rationale: The update log card sat empty on every launch; a failed driver update now opens a dialog with the tail of its output instead.

nodes.label: Fifth round: Defrag as one card per OS group
nodes.rationale: Tiles lost their own individual cards; each OS group is now a single card with wider spacing so tiles stay apart without borders.

nodes.label: Windows port (windows/)
A sibling tree, not one cross-platform package
nodes.rationale: windows/ shares architecture (models.py, risk.py, leftovers.py, scanner.py, uninstaller.py, backends/) but almost no code with linux/, since every leaf is platform-specific.

nodes.label: GUI: tkinter, not GTK3
nodes.rationale: tkinter is in the Windows Python stdlib and costs nothing to freeze with PyInstaller, unlike shipping an MSYS2 GTK runtime; costs a custom filter model and checkbox renderer.

nodes.label: GUI look: 'Graphite & Signal'
nodes.rationale: Dark graphite palette with one lime accent, built from a mockup rather than chasing a native Fluent look clam can't reach; disk-space bar doubles as the source filter.

nodes.label: Four sources, and why winget isn't one
nodes.rationale: winget install hands off to the program's own MSI/EXE installer which writes the same Uninstall key already read from the registry; adding winget would double-list every app.

nodes.label: Reading Chocolatey/Scoop off disk, not calling their CLIs
nodes.rationale: Faster than a process per scan and the file layout (nuspec, manifest.json) is far more stable than choco list's CLI contract, which broke across a major version.

nodes.label: Privilege escalation: ShellExecuteEx + runas, not sudo
nodes.rationale: UAC is a property of how a process is launched; elevate.py uses ShellExecuteExW via ctypes with SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS so the exit code can be waited on and read.

nodes.label: Output goes to files, not pipes
nodes.rationale: capture_output reads to EOF, which never arrives if an uninstaller spawns a child (browser page) that inherits the pipe; file handles wait only for the uninstaller's own exit.

nodes.label: Fix: split_command crashed every registry uninstall
nodes.rationale: CommandLineToArgvW called with ctypes' default int restype truncated the returned pointer; fixed by declaring argtypes/restype, and the worker now catches and reports exceptions.

nodes.label: Hand-off uninstallers: follow the process tree, ask the registry
nodes.rationale: Inno/NSIS launchers copy themselves to TEMP and exit, so waiting on the launcher alone finishes too early; a Toolhelp32 snapshot every 0.1-0.5s traces the whole family, and success is read from the registry key, not the exit code.

nodes.label: Risk heuristic: registry fields, same as Linux reads dpkg
nodes.rationale: SystemComponent/ReleaseType/driver-name patterns decide Critical/Caution without a reverse-dependency scan; exit code 1605 (ERROR_UNKNOWN_PRODUCT) is treated as success.

nodes.label: Leftovers: AppData/ProgramData, not Documents or registry
nodes.rationale: Documents holds the user's own files and a name match there risks offering to delete real work; registry leftovers are deferred pending their own confirmation UI.

nodes.label: Taskbar identity: SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID
nodes.rationale: The shell groups taskbar buttons by AppUserModelID, defaulting to the host exe; it must be set before any window exists because Windows caches the decision.

nodes.label: The .ico is generated from the same curves by a stdlib script
nodes.rationale: make_icon.py re-evaluates icon.svg's cubic beziers as stroked capsules, supersamples and box-filters, and writes the ICO container itself with struct/zlib, avoiding a rasterizer dependency.

nodes.label: Build: PyInstaller for .exe, WiX for .msi, on a Windows runner
nodes.rationale: cx_Freeze's MSI support is weaker and Inno/NSIS can't produce the .msi group policy deployment needs; WiX is pinned to 5.0.2 since 7 requires accepting a maintenance-fee EULA.

nodes.label: run.py exists because a frozen __main__ isn't a package member
nodes.rationale: PyInstaller runs the entry script as __main__ with no package to resolve relative imports against, so a three-line absolute-import shim is needed.

nodes.label: Windows: the Stitches design and tools (0.2.0)
Windows Updates: Windows Update, winget, Chocolatey, Scoop
nodes.rationale: winget is a source here (unlike Uninstall) because its upgrade feed is the only thing that knows a newer version of an ordinary installer exists, like a vendor apt repo.

nodes.label: Windows Cleanup locations
nodes.rationale: Thumbnails are excluded because Explorer always holds thumbcache files open; a cell's text is now fitted to leave room for the risk tag that follows it.

nodes.label: Windows Drivers via Win32_PnPSignedDriver + Windows Update
nodes.rationale: One place to ask, unlike Linux's three; devices made up in software (ROOT\, SWD\) are excluded, and an update is matched to its device by DriverModel.

nodes.label: Windows Defrag via Optimize-Volume
nodes.rationale: Optimize-Volume defragments hard disks and TRIMs SSDs itself, so unlike Linux an SSD is something to do, not skip; tiles are grouped by disk letter.

nodes.label: Windows Diagnose: the tools themselves, not stand-ins
nodes.rationale: Windows has the real tools (Get-PhysicalDisk, Get-Volume) so checks name the tool directly; sfc and DISM can't even look without admin rights so they're Info rows with a fix.

nodes.label: Windows self-update: .msi, portable exe, or git checkout
nodes.rationale: Install path is decided from sys.executable's location; a running portable exe is renamed to .old rather than overwritten, then the new one started with PYINSTALLER_RESET_ENVIRONMENT=1.

nodes.label: Two Tk traps the first CI run caught
nodes.rationale: THEME must start as the Dark palette (not empty) since a Table redraw can run before the saved theme applies; the update notice ActionBar needs tk.Misc.lift, not Canvas.lift.

nodes.label: Bug: every elevated action failed in 0.2.3
nodes.rationale: tempfile.mkdtemp's Windows ACL (since Python 3.12.4) makes an elevated process own the output file our token can't read; fixed with log.touch() before launch so we own it. -EncodedCommand also surfaced PowerShell errors as CLIXML, fixed by running a UTF-8-BOM .ps1 instead.

nodes.label: Android port (android/)
A third sibling tree, one place the shape breaks
nodes.rationale: Android has exactly one register of installed software, so unlike Linux/Windows a backends/ directory with a Backend protocol would hold one file; Scanner.kt/Sources.kt handle it directly instead.

nodes.label: Kotlin, platform's own widgets: no AndroidX, no Compose
nodes.rationale: android.widget is already in every device's system image; the release APK is 57KB versus two orders of magnitude for a stock Compose/Material app of the same scope.

nodes.label: The gap is a different shape, and the docs say so
nodes.rationale: Android Settings already lists every installed app, so the honest pitch is what it doesn't do: show install source, bulk-remove, warn about your keyboard, or clean leftover folders.

nodes.label: Five sources out of one field (getInstallSourceInfo)
nodes.rationale: An unrecognised installer is labelled a store (not sideloaded), since a fixed known-list would mislabel every vendor store on the market; FLAG_SYSTEM wins over the installer tag.

nodes.label: Privilege escalation: the system's own uninstall dialog
nodes.rationale: Intent.ACTION_DELETE is the only API a normal app has; this forces one dialog per app, so bulk selection becomes a queue of sequential removals via onActivityResult.

nodes.label: 'Did it go?' asked of the package manager, not the result code
nodes.rationale: resultCode is ignored outright; getApplicationInfo with MATCH_DISABLED_COMPONENTS reports the real outcome, making 'disabled' a distinguishable third state from 'still installed'.

nodes.label: Preinstalled apps get App Info, not ACTION_DELETE
nodes.rationale: ACTION_DELETE on a system app either silently removes just the update or does nothing; Disable/Uninstall-updates are the only real verbs, and disabled apps are excluded from freed-space totals.

nodes.label: Risk heuristic: three authoritative signals, one name pattern
nodes.rationale: Default launcher, active device admins and active keyboard are facts (one query per scan each) rather than guesses; core-vs-vendor-preinstall split is the only remaining guess.

nodes.label: Leftovers: shared storage only, never media folders
nodes.rationale: Android already deletes /data/data and Android/data|obb on uninstall; media folders (DCIM, Pictures, Music) are excluded to avoid offering to delete someone's photos on a name collision.

nodes.label: Two optional permissions, both skippable, neither assumed
nodes.rationale: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS are special-access permissions reachable only via a Settings screen; the app degrades gracefully without either rather than requiring them.

nodes.label: QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES is why the release is an APK, not Play
nodes.rationale: Listing every installed app is the whole product, ruling out a declared <queries> list; Play restricts QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, so the release artifact is a signed APK on GitHub Releases instead.

nodes.label: Health check: what an app can see, and nothing it can't
nodes.rationale: Verified boot state leads the list as Android's answer to sfc /scannow; each verdict is a pure function in Health.kt over plain values, testable on the JVM.

nodes.label: The icon is the same path data, not a second drawing
nodes.rationale: Vector drawables take SVG path data verbatim, so icon.svg's curves are copied as-is with no rasteriser or generator script needed, superseded once the logo was sewn.

nodes.label: Build: Gradle and R8 on any machine, with a key that must exist
nodes.rationale: android-build.yml exists for the signing key, not the platform; an unsigned or throwaway-signed release is treated as worse than no release, so the workflow fails outright if the secret is missing.

nodes.label: The Stitches design (Android)
The sewn logo needs a generator (make_logo.py)
nodes.rationale: Vector drawables have no stroke-dasharray, so make_logo.py samples each curve and cuts it into dash polylines simplified with Ramer-Douglas-Peucker to match the Linux logo.

hyperedges.label: Use the platform's own already-installed UI toolkit (GTK3 / tkinter / android.widget)
Trust the authoritative state (dpkg status / registry key / package manager) over a process exit code
CLAUDE.md privilege-escalation non-negotiable, realized per platform (pkexec / ShellExecuteEx+runas / system uninstall dialog)
